chunks: And by this chain, from Fadala, from Aban, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding
a man who prayed the morning prayer at night, the moon having deceived him, and he slept until the sun rose; then he was informed that he had prayed at night. He said: He must repeat his prayer.

key_terms.غَرَّهُ: Deceived/misled him — refers to the moon's brightness mimicking dawn light
key_terms.يعيد: To repeat, to redo — legal technical term for invalidated acts of worship

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone prays Fajr at night thinking it is dawn?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who mistakenly prayed the Fajr (dawn) prayer at night, deceived by the brightness of the moon into thinking it was dawn, then slept until after sunrise. The Imam issued a clear ruling that the prayer must be repeated (i'ada), as it was performed outside its prescribed time. This ruling reflects the jurisprudential principle that prayer performed before its designated time is invalid and must be redone.

en.hubeali:
And by this chain, from Fazalat, from Aban, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding

a man who prayed the morning Salāt at night, the moon (light) having deceived him from that, and he slept until the emergence of the sun. So he was informed that he had prayed at night’. Heasws said: ‘He should repeat his Salāt’.
en.sarwar: 4. Through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith it is narrated from Fadalah from Aban from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about

a man who performs the morning Salah (prayer) during the night mistakenly because of moon light and then goes to sleep until sunrise and he then is informed of having performed his morning Salah (prayer) during the night, has said, ‘He must perform it again.’”
